item.title: Mowers, Sweepers, and a Nine-Quarter Slump: The Case for Alamo Group
item.description: A $2 billion industrial manufacturer just posted an earnings beat, closed a bolt-on acquisition, and got a tariff-relief tailwind -- and almost nobody's talking about it. Alex and Jordan dig into Alamo Group's mowers-and-sewer-trucks business, break down two quarters of results, and explain why 'boring but essential' might be exactly what makes this stock interesting right now.

item.title: The Foam Company Quietly Printing Record Profits: UFP Technologies
item.description: A $2.5 billion medical device contract manufacturer just posted record earnings and beat estimates by double digits, sending shares up over 11% -- and almost nobody noticed. Alex and Jordan dig into UFP Technologies, the unglamorous foam-and-plastics company quietly powering hospital supply chains, and explain why this steady compounder still flies under Wall Street's radar.

item.title: The Marine Contractor Nobody's Watching: Digging Into Orion Group Holdings (ORN)
item.description: This week we're heading to the docks with Orion Group Holdings, a Houston-based specialty construction company that builds ports, Navy facilities, and marine infrastructure most investors have never heard of. We break down a rough Q2 print, a price-target cut, and why this $379 million small-cap is exactly the kind of name that flies under the radar until it doesn't.

item.title: The Tractor Turnaround Nobody's Watching: Titan Machinery's Quiet Margin Story
item.description: Revenue is still falling double digits, but gross margins just hit their best levels in years. We dig into Titan Machinery, a small-cap farm and construction equipment dealer working through a brutal ag downturn while quietly executing an inventory turnaround that Wall Street's technicals haven't caught up to yet.

item.title: Costco, Cracker Barrel, and a Trump-Xi Summit: Your Week Ahead
item.description: A packed week of earnings from Costco, Darden, Lennar, and AutoZone lands right after the Fed's September meeting, alongside fresh housing and sentiment data. Alex and Jordan map out what to watch, including the high-stakes Trump-Xi summit that could move markets either direction.

item.title: The Truck Company Riding the Grid Boom Nobody's Watching
item.description: H&E Equipment got bought out, so we found the next best thing: Custom Truck One Source, a $2.5 billion specialty rental and manufacturing company quietly posting double-digit growth off the electric grid buildout. We break down two straight guidance raises, a looming emissions-rule twist, and why almost nobody's talking about this one yet.

item.title: The Modular Building Company Quietly Riding the AI Boom
item.description: McGrath RentCorp rents modular buildings and portable storage to schools and contractors — not exactly a headline-grabbing business. But buried inside its earnings is a test-equipment segment growing double digits on data center and AI infrastructure demand, a 33-year dividend growth streak, and a stock trading well below analysts' fair value estimate. Alex and Jordan dig into why nobody's talking about this one.

item.title: The Workers' Comp Company That Bought Back 70% of Itself
item.description: Everyone's ignoring CorVel Corporation, a debt-free, thirty-year compounder in the unglamorous world of workers' comp claims management and medical bill repricing. We dig into why revenue growth just reaccelerated to 11%, why the stock is still down nearly 50% over the past year, and why almost nobody is talking about it.

item.title: The Fed Finally Pulls the Trigger: Rate Hikes Are Back
item.description: The Fed hikes rates for the first time since 2023, Treasury yields punch through levels not seen since 2007, and Wall Street spends the week trying to figure out if this is a one-and-done move or the start of something longer. Alex and Jordan break down the FOMC decision, a wild divergence between the Dow and the Nasdaq, Netflix's ugly downgrade, and why small-cap stocks are having a moment nobody's talking about.
